title: My First HTML Page
description: Build a complete HTML page with a title, a paragraph of text, and an interactive button.
starterHTML:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>My Page</title>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Write your code below -->

</body>
</html>

steps.title: Add a Heading
steps.instructions: Add an <h1> element inside the <body> with the text 'Hello World'. A heading is the main title of your page.

quiz.question: Which HTML tag is used for the main heading of a page?
quiz.explanation: <h1> defines the most important heading. There should be only one per page.

quiz.question: Where should you place the <h1> tag?
quiz.explanation: All visible content, including headings, goes inside the <body> tag.

steps.title: Add a Paragraph
steps.instructions:
Below your heading, add a

element with a sentence describing yourself or your page.

quiz.question:
What does the

tag stand for?
quiz.explanation: stands for paragraph. It creates a block of text with spacing above and below.

steps.title: Add a Button
steps.instructions: Finally, add a <button> element below your paragraph. Give it the text 'Click Me!'.

quiz.question: What does the <button> tag create?
quiz.explanation: The <button> tag creates a clickable button. It can trigger JavaScript events or submit forms.

quiz.question: Which attribute adds a tooltip to a button?
quiz.explanation: The title attribute shows a tooltip when hovering. Example: <button title="Click to submit">

title: HTML Forms Basics
description: Create an HTML form with inputs, labels, and a submit button.
starterHTML: Contact Us

steps.title: Create the Form Skeleton
steps.instructions: Add a <form> element with action='#' and method='post'. This is the container for all your inputs.

quiz.question: What attribute specifies where form data is sent?
quiz.explanation: The action attribute specifies the URL where the form data is submitted.

steps.title: Add Name & Email Inputs
steps.instructions: Inside the form, add two <input> elements: one for name (type='text') and one for email (type='email'). Each should have a <label>.

quiz.question: Which input type automatically validates email format in the browser?
quiz.explanation: type="email" triggers built-in browser validation to check for proper email format.

steps.title: Add a Submit Button
steps.instructions: Add a <button type='submit'> at the end of the form. Style it with an inline style if you like.

quiz.question: What type of button submits a form?
quiz.explanation: type="submit" sends the form data. type="reset" clears all fields. type="button" does nothing by default.

title: CSS Styling Fundamentals
description: Style an HTML page using both inline styles and a <style> block.
starterHTML:
My Styled Page

This page needs styling!

This is a card component.

steps.title: Add a Style Block
steps.instructions: Inside <head>, add a <style> tag and set body { font-family: sans-serif; background: #f0f0f0; }

quiz.question: Where should the <style> tag be placed?
quiz.explanation: CSS <style> blocks go in the <head> section so styles load before the page content renders.

steps.title: Style the Heading
steps.instructions: In your style block, style h1 with color: #2c3e50 and text-align: center.

quiz.question: Which CSS property centers text horizontally in its container?
quiz.explanation: text-align: center is the correct CSS property for horizontal text alignment.
